reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes depositing Bitcoin into Mirror Trading International while making earnings depend on recruiting people into left and right legs of a binary team structure. It combines a minimum $100 contribution, seven-day urgency, downline-based commissions, and claims that members can make substantial or continuous Bitcoin income, encouraging viewers to join and fund the platform.

opening.argument: The speaker does not present Bitcoin as risk-free or certain. He expressly acknowledges that Bitcoin can move substantially in either direction: "Bitcoin fluctuate 10 to 20 percent. It can go up or it can go down." That is a meaningful uncertainty warning, and the description's language about earning daily is not the same as a guarantee of profit. The presentation also contrasts its claimed fee structure with other companies rather than promising a fixed return. On this record, the financial discussion can reasonably be understood as conditional commentary about a volatile asset and a proposed trading service, not deceptive certification that viewers will definitely profit.

citations.quote: Bitcoin fluctuate 10 to 20 percent. It can go up or it can go down.
Everything that you make, you will be able to pull out without worrying about paying any fees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes the $100 contribution, recruitment structure, and income language, but those points do not eliminate the speaker's explicit acknowledgment that Bitcoin may rise or fall. Referral compensation and a trading-pool contribution may be features of a promoted service without proving that the speaker concealed market risk or guaranteed a particular return.

citations.quote: the minimum we're asking people to join, like I said before, was $100 in Bitcoin
Bitcoin fluctuate 10 to 20 percent. It can go up or it can go down.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Acknowledging that Bitcoin fluctuates does not cure the promotional claims. The speaker still says the company had made Bitcoin for members every day and describes people being able to make great money from new members placed under them. A general volatility statement does not explain the risks of the pool or the recruitment-dependent compensation.

opening.argument: The video's stated function is to update viewers and explain how the platform works. The speaker says he wants to provide an update, responds to questions about how it works, and says he will go over relevant details. The material then walks through practical onboarding concepts such as obtaining a wallet, registering, funding, and choosing a team position. That structure is consistent with an operational explainer or business-process demonstration. Explaining a system and its terminology does not by itself establish that the system is fraudulent, especially where the speaker presents the information as an update rather than as an investigation or a concealed transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution reads the instructional portions as solicitation, but instructional detail is also what viewers would need to understand an unfamiliar platform. The speaker explains wallet setup, registration, funding, and placement mechanics in response to questions, which supports an educational or operational reading even if the underlying service is not independently verified here.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The content is not merely a neutral explanation. The speaker tells viewers what amount to put in, which side to choose, and when to act to preserve their position. He also says new people can end up under the viewer and generate money. Those direct participation instructions make the video promotional, and an explainer format does not negate that function.

opening.argument: The observable offer can be framed as a service with ordinary onboarding and a referral component, not as proof of a scam mechanism. The speaker describes free membership with no subscriptions, packages, costs, or deductions, and separately describes a Bitcoin wallet, registration, and a minimum contribution. The sampled material presents those steps as a branded service process. Nothing supplied establishes a credential request, a fabricated identity, or a verified outcome; the existence or performance of the trading pool is not independently demonstrated by these materials. The evidence therefore supports promotion of a Bitcoin-related service, while leaving the decisive safety question unresolved.

citations.quote: when you become a free member there's no subscriptions no packages no costs no deductions
make sure you get you got you a bitcoin wallet
Register with MTI

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the referral arrangement and contribution as a scam mechanism, but a referral structure can also accompany ordinary service promotion. The supplied material does not independently establish that the pool is fictitious, that funds cannot be withdrawn, or that the service has no trading activity. The absence of those decisive facts makes a non-scam service classification reasonable on this record.

citations.quote: you can pretty much put in your Bitcoin and put it right into the trading pool without any fees

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not whether a service could use referrals; it is how earnings are represented here. The speaker explicitly ties binary funds to people he brings into the company and urges viewers to join before others get ahead of them. Those statements show recruitment-dependent income and a funded entry requirement, even if the materials do not independently prove whether the pool exists.
